items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: So Dickie, myself, Mack Walker, Harold McFerran, and Don Frye got together again with 'Bull' Williams... So Beasley had a 9-piece orchestra to take to Poughkeepsie.

ctx.x: We were saved by a miracle. The ditch we went into was about 5 inches deep at this particular place. Our car went over on the left side and bounced back onto the road. We were shaking like falling leaves when the driver stopped the car. The miracle was that just a few feet from where we went over, there was a ditch about 3 feet deep. The only damage/that was was done was the rack that was on the left running board in which there were some bags was torn off and John William's bag was busted. The car had only a…

In Lousiville we played a big dance and stayed there a few days. All of Dickie's friends came to the dance and there was no question of us paying for all the juice that was passed to us. I and most of those in the band that drank could carry the load so we were never drunk while working. Bull Williams, the ex-football player, didn't drink and Harold "Hoggie" McFerran drank very little.

There was a bar in Louisville that I had known from the first time I had gone there with Helvey, which was very popular with musicians and entertainers because one could get the best home cooked beans that were ever cooked in this place. For 5 cents you had a big bowl of beans, 5 cents was also the price of a pair of hot dogs and the same price for a big mug of beer.
